utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Since there are no procedural issues raised, may I take it, Mr. Re, that you are ready to call your next witness, who is in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. I call Mr. Jose Antonio Lorenzo Quiroz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re. Mr. Quiroz, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make the solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by the usher. I invite you to make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Quiroz. Please be seated. You'll first be examined by Mr. Re, who's counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Quiroz. Your name is Jose Antonio Lorenzo Quiroz. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is it Mr. Lorenzo Quiroz, Mr. Quiroz or Mr. Lorenzo?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: It's Mr. Lorenzo Quiroz.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your date of birth is the 29th of October, 1975.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were an investigator at the ICTY from September 2003 until July 2005. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before that, where did you work?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I was working in Spain. Previously I had been with the United Nations mission in East Timor, working as an investigator for the serious crimes unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you a police investigator in Spain?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But you now work at the International Criminal Court.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just tell the Trial Chamber briefly what the extent of your role was in the investigations in this case.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: When I first arrived here at the Tribunal, I was assigned to a team which investigated the crimes that were committed in the territory of Kosovo, and particularly by the KLA leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your duties include interviewing witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, they would include interviewing the witnesses, and suspects as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: In Kosovo and in other theatres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you did that, did you take interpreters with you?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your role in the compilation of photo identification boards?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I was tasked to compile photo-boards, and for this I basically followed the standard operational procedures. I took eight photographs from a collection which we had which was obtained through an international organisation. Basically it was a compilation of the Kosovo Protection Corps' database, and from there I selected photographs which were as close as possible to those of the suspects that had been identified at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The international organisation, was that in Kosovo, the one that provided the photographs to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe so. I was not involved in the collection, but from review -- it was in our database and I believe it was two investigators that were prior to me working at the organisation that had collected those from Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you took eight. How did you find the eight?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: The first step I took was to obtain a photograph of the suspect, and then I went through both the electronic copy, which we had, and a print-out copy of the photographs and looked for pictures that were similar in all aspects in that the person in the photograph was as closely as possible -- looked as closely as possible to the suspects, and with similar backgrounds, if possible, and same size, same postures. Usually the photographs were from shoulder up, passport-type, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Approximately how many photographs do you remember or do you think that you looked at in this process of compiling these photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: There were thousands. Thousands of photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did it take you to do it?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but it took several weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who actually put the photographs onto the boards?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I downloaded electronic versions of the photographs that were available and put them on a layout of an A4 paper, laid horizontally and 4 and 4, so it would be a total of eight photographs. I did the digital part of that. I later sent that to the mapping and printing section of the OTP for further editing. So the backgrounds would be the same and any marks that were on the photographs would be eliminated and try to make them as similar as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many photo-boards did you compile in the sense of how many boards containing suspects were there?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe six. I could name them. That will probably be easier if I name them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I compiled one for the defendant here, Ramush Haradinaj; for his two brothers, Mr. Daut Haradinaj -- one of his other brothers, I believe it's Shkelzen Haradinaj. Excuse my pronunciation. For the other defendants, Lahi Brahimaj. For Alush Agushi, and Pjeter Shala, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Nazmi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: As well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Idriz Balaj, also known as Toger?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I did not compile that one. I was involved in -- that was compiled by another investigator, who sent the electronic copy to me which I forwarded to the mapping section, printing and mapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was that investigator?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe it was Pekka Havarinen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you put eight photographs on a board. How many variations were there of each of the eight photographs, or eight sets containing one suspect?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: As I said, I sent these photographs to the mapping and printing section. I never indicated to them which one of the photographs was the suspect and I just asked them to print out three different copies -- once they were adjusted, to print out three different sets with all the photographs scrambled. On some occasions I had to send the board back because the photographs were scrambled but the suspect's photo remained in the same spot, so I had to ask for that one to be changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some photographs, starting with 65 ter Exhibit 1135.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And for the court officer, 1136, 1138, 11 -- I'm sorry, did I say 7? 1137, 1138, 1139, 1140, and 1141, so if those could be shown in that order, please, starting with 1135. All right. Could you please go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that a photo-board in relation to Alush Agushi that you compiled?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be given a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P359, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Registrar. Any objection against admission? I take it you want to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, there is no objection to this and no objection to the ensuing photo-boards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that would be different for other counsel, I would like to hear. Then P359 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It may be quicker if I hand the other six to the witness and get a number afterwards because it's taking a few moments for it to load now, if there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can hand them to the witness. May I take it that you are handing them in the order as you just indicated, that is, to start with 1137 up to 1141 because that would then be 1137, 359 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1136 is then 359; 1137 would be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P360, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would be P361.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would be P362.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be P363 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just going to show the documents which Mr. Registrar has just read on to the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Firstly is 1136, the 36 you compiled for Daut Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to avoid confusion, the transcript reads that you started with 1135, Mr. Re, and that would be 359.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So not 1136. Mr. Registrar, would you move up all the numbers. That means 1136 becomes 360; 1137, 361; 1138, 362; 1139, 363; 1140, 36 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 364, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because the transcript is not -- and then 1141 would be 365. And let's forget what the end of page 6 and the beginning of page 7 said before. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Starting at the three sets for Daut Haradinaj, which is 1136, which is now Exhibit P39; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I think it was just corrected now to be 360.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you look at line -- page 7, line 15, Mr. Re, you'll find the new order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Becomes 360, it reads on line 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I'm sorry, I was reading the old one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: P360, Daut Haradinaj, is correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll move to the next one, 1137, which is P361, which is three sets for Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that correct. The next one is 362, which is Nazmi Brahimaj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one is 363, which is Pjeter Shala. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one is 1140, is that Idriz Balaj, which is 364?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, this is --

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: This is Idriz Balaj. This one, as I mentioned, I was only involved in forwarding them on to the mapping section.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the final one is three sets for Lahi Brahimaj, which is P365?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you show any photo-boards to witnesses in the course of your interviewing them?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Trial Chamber about the procedures you -- first of all, how many witnesses, approximately, did you show photo -- these photo identification boards to in the process of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Very, very few. I can't say a number because I don't know, but it would be less than five, for sure, two, three maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what were the procedures you employed? What did you do when you showed the photo-boards to witnesses? What was your practice?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I would show the photo-boards during the course of an interview. During -- I would start by interviewing the witness and -- and asking of him about --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, if rather than a practice we could have specifically what the officer, I think it might be of more assistance. Considering there are so few photo-boards that he showed, he could us specifically what he did with a witness rather than a custom of what he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, let's first hear the answer of the witness, and then we of course could ask him whether this was a uniform practice or whether there was any variety.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you would start by interviewing the witness and asking him about ...

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Just about the events. In the course of the interview, a witness may or may have not mentioned one of the suspects. And if they did I would explore all of the circumstances around this event, what they knew, the prior knowledge, and if they've ever seen the perpetrator or the alleged perpetrator, suspect, prior or after the event. And I would continue with the interview. And at some stage later on I would show a photo-board. I would tell the witness that I was going to show them a photo-board, and I would lay it out in front of them and ask them to have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the procedure you employed in laying it out in front of them? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I would just place it in front of them. I would step back or move aside and I would let the witnesses have a look at it. There's not much more.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the procedure in recording what a witness said?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I would usually -- I would record it in the -- in the body of the statement. I say "usually," because I know that there has been one time which I did not follow this practice, and I believe I'll be questioned regarding this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll come to that in a moment, but let's just go back to your practice, and if a witness made a positive or a negative identification, that is, no identification or a positive identification, what did you do with the photograph, or what did you get the witness to do with the forcible transfer?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I would ask the witness to circle a number and to sign on -- on the board. And I would include that in -- in the body of the statement. I would include any other circumstance that the witness would -- would mention surrounding the identification or comments they may have made during the practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you aware of the Office of the Prosecutor's photo-board identification guide-lines?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For photographic procedures. Now, they include a thing called a photo identification -- sorry, a photo-board identification procedure report, which according to the guide-lines is supposed to be completed by investigators and the investigator is supposed to prepare a statement and annex it to that report. What was your practice in relation to completing the report which is in the OTP's guide-lines?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I did not prepare that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you never prepare that -- such a report?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about other investigators working in this case, are you aware whether they were doing -- preparing reports or not?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you able to give the Court a reason why the reports weren't being prepared?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: They're -- I can't give a reason. It's disresulted, burdensome, and when there was a duplication of what was already added in the statement itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to take you to two witnesses you identified -- sorry, not identified, interviewed, and I want to show you two exhibits under seal. Firstly, P23; and secondly, Exhibit P15.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: They're under seal so they shouldn't be displayed to the public, but they're the pseudonyms and the witnesses' names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, I take it that the documents will not be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, is there anyone in the public gallery? Yes. Then we have to pull the curtains down for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When we refer to the witnesses in court, Mr. Lorenzo Quiroz, I just want to refer to them by their pseudonyms, that's Witness 4 and Witness 19, but I'm showing you these for identification purposes so you're completely clear who we're talking about. Okay, you see Witness 4 and you see the name of Witness 4?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown P15, that's the pseudonym sheet for Witness 19. Okay. Thank you. It no longer need be displayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the curtains may be pulled up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, did you interview Witness 4 on the 21st of October, 2004, in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you show him the photo-board which is Exhibit P27 containing a photograph of the accused Idriz Balaj?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I did show a photograph, but I believe it was in June when I interviewed the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right. Perhaps if I could show you a copy of the witness's statement which is 65 ter 1397.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, at this juncture --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- I would object unless there's a reason for doing so. He's indicated he did show him the photo-board, and he gave a date on which he did it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe there may be some dissatisfaction with the response and rather than leading occurring at this point, I think the matter should be examined in another fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's hardly a memory test three years later as to the date you showed a witness a photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This should be displayed under seal; it has the witness's identifying details on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we again have to pull down the curtains.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you could just look at the witness statement which is on the screen there which refers to Witness 4, the date of the interview is recorded as the 21st of October, 2004. A moment ago I think you said you showed the witness the photographs in June.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I can -- I might be mistaken. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness be -- can you please go to paragraph -- sorry, page 9, which is U0083820.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You see paragraph 75 which says: "At this stage the investigator has now shown me a spreadsheet containing eight different photographs of individuals," and so on. "After having a close look I must state that the picture number 6 is the man I know as Idriz Balaj, a.k.a. 'Togeri.' I have signed the spreadsheet and attached it to my statement." And there's a signature at the bottom of the page. Does that assist you with the date at which you showed the witness the photographs?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: This was definitely shown to him in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And if you can go two pages along, please, Mr. Registrar, to the last page U0083822, which is in fact Exhibit P27.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want you to confirm that that is the photograph you showed Witness 4 bearing his signature with the circle around number 6?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, this is the board.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, when you showed him these photographs, did you adopt your usual procedures?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I would have.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was with you when you showed the photograph to him? Did you have an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I did have an interpreter. This in -- yeah, I -- yes, I did. I could name the interpreter, I think, I. Can I name him?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I think it was Maklen Misha, but I cannot tell by the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The front page records it as having been Mr. Maklen Misha, assuming that's correct was there anybody with you with Witness 4 when you interviewed?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe not. It should have been recorded -- it would have been recorded on the front page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say you believe not, do you have any memory of it or are you relying on your usual practice?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I'm relying on my usual practice and the fact that this was October 2004 which was quite a long mission, it was a three-week mission if I recall, and all the investigators that were there were tasked with several duties, and we wouldn't have really had time to be doing too many interviews at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: During that mission did you also interview the witness's brother, that's Witness 19?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes. They were both interviewed if -- not on the same day but one was interviewed first and the other was interviewed on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit D9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Again it's under seal, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, the -- Mr. Registrar puts the same question to me that came into my mind. What do you want to do with 65 ter 1397, do you consider, if the parties agree, that the front page is given the date in October and that you read the relevant portion of it, there might be no need to tender it. I'm looking at Defence counsel, whether they would have any problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, we would not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there's no need to mark it for identification. Please proceed. D9 is now under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. I have a paper copy which may speed things up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You could give it -- well, it's on the screen already, but.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This is a statement of the brother, that is, Witness 19, recorded as having taken place on the 18th of July and the 20th of October, 2004. Your name is on the front. One interpreter is there on the 18th of July, 2004, Mr. Maklen Misha is recorded as having been there on the 20th of October, 2004. Now, do you remember taking this statement from Witness 19?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to turn to page 7, paragraphs 52, 53, and 54. Which start: "Questioned by the investigator how I know that the soldier that I know as Idriz Balaj, a.k.a. 'Toger' is in fact who I say it is, I must say even though I was a small child at the time I remember his face." And at paragraph 53 he is recorded as saying: "I am certain that this man I know as Idriz Balaj, a.k.a. 'Toger' is the same man that abducted my sister ..." Now, what I want to ask you about is the procedure there that you employed. You said you showed him photographs of Idriz Balaj. Did you show Witness 19 a photo-identification board containing a variation of the same pictures of Idriz Balaj?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, that's not recorded in this statement?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you provide the Court with an explanation as to why that's not in the statement?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: First of all, the showing of the photographs to him and then whatever the witness might have said?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall this. And the photographs were shown during the June interview, not during this interview in October. Things were confusing at the time. I remember going up to the village -- I'm just providing a bit of a history, going to their village and asking around for them, and I left a phone number on a piece of blank paper for the witness to contact. The witness contacted us and came to Pristina to be interviewed -- to meet us, because at the time the witness was not informed who we were. It was only after that I met with the witness that I explained to him and to his brother, who were present as well, and their grandmother who we were and why we wanted to meet them. This occurred in the office, and we sat in one of the offices together and we established an initial rapport between us. And there they started telling me a bit about what had occurred. At a moment in time, the witness's grandmother became very emotionally disturbed, and I asked one of the witnesses that I've interviewed later on to sit with her in a different room. And it was during that time where I stayed with -- I'm sorry, I can't remember if it's 4 or 19, it's the younger of the two brothers. I stayed with him in the office, and I conducted the initial interview, just asking questions. And at one stage towards -- I think it was during the read-back, I had shown the photograph -- the photo-board to the witness, but at the time the witness was not asked to sign a statement because they both showed serious concerns about their safety and their security. And I -- I'm sorry. And I just forgot about that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So you showed the photographs to both brothers, but you recorded the details in Witness 4's statement but not Witness 19's statement.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: With Witness 19, I was always a bit puzzled with their -- what they were saying, and I'm basing myself on the age that they had when this occurred. I wasn't sure if I was -- I never thought of showing them the photograph initially and I wasn't going to show it. But I did at the end of the interview. I can't remember whether I showed the other brother the photograph then or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just to be clear, with Witness 19 I think you said June, you did it in June. The statement says -- doesn't record you as having spoken to him in June.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Well, at the time I did speak was when the whole family was there. It was the two brothers and the grandmother. We were just talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you when you showed him the photograph? Was it in the village or in the office in Pristina or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: It was in the office. The village was too dangerous to -- dangerous for their security. They would have easily been identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did Witness 19 say when you showed the photograph to him?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he made a negative or a positive identification?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I barely remember the incident at all. The only reason I mentioned it now and I have come to know about it was because of the day the witness was giving testimony in court, I received a phone call from one of the investigators asking whether I had shown the witness a photograph or not, and I just said, It will be in the statement, because that's what I believed. And the investigator later informed me that it wasn't. So I started looking through my diaries and trying to remember, and I did show the witness a photograph but I just ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have you recorded anywhere --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one follow-up question first. You said, "I received a phone call from one of the investigators." When did you receive that phone call?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the day that the witness was in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember more details?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was -- I received the call on my mobile phone and I was out of the office, so I was out for a walk at lunchtime. I would say it was about 1.00 or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did he tell you, the investigator? Did he just put this question to you or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The investigator asked me whether I had shown a photo-board to this witness or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And just told me to take my time and to think about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he also tell you why he put that question to you at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The investigator said that the witness had said in court, here during his testimony, that I had shown him the photo-board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember who the investigator was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It was Thomas Obruca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you at any later stage have any contact with one of the investigators or one of the persons employed in the Office of the Prosecution on this matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I called the investigator back two days after this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and the investigator told me that he could not speak about the matter. He said -- this was over the weekend, I recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And he informed me that I may wish to speak to one of the legal officers on the team. So I called one of the trial attorneys on Monday -- to the same trial attorney I spoke to, asked me if I was contacting him for -- it if had anything to do with my time at the ICTY, and I said yes. And the trial attorney informed me that they were ordered not to talk to me about this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I was going to ask you, did you -- you said you went back -- you said: "I started looking through my diaries and trying to remember and I did show the witness a photograph, but I just" -- and I was going to ask you: Did you record the fact that you'd shown the witness a photograph? Did you record it anywhere?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No, it's not recorded. In my diary, the only thing I had was a note of the witness's name, and two days later, a day later, I had a note that I faxed through -- whatever I typed up at the moment, I faxed it through here to the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, who was present in the room with you when you showed the photograph to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: It would have been the interpreter. That's the one that's on the first page of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were the two brothers ever together when you interviewed them or showed them the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: They were together at the initial stage when we were just -- when I was explaining to them the reason why I wanted to meet with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just stop there. Was that in the village?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No, not in the village. In the village, I went up to the village, and in the village I asked around. Nobody knew about them, so I just left a number, a telephone number, and asked them to contact me and they did. It was in the office. In the office, I have only asked for two -- I have only asked for the grandmother and one of the brothers. The identity of the other brother was unknown to me at that stage. I thought that individual had been killed in the shooting incident in March -- March that year, 1998 I believe it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said they were together at the initial stage when you were explaining the reason why you wanted to meet with them. Just to be clear, was that in the office in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For approximately how long were they and the grandmother there while you explained this to them?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I cannot say. Maybe half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the formal interviewing process? Were the two brothers ever together during the formal interviewing process?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No. They were separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about when you showed them the photographs? Were they together or were they separate?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: They were separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re. Who will be first to cross-examine the witness? Mr. Emmerson, I see you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have just one or two questions. I'll be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel for Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you one or two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the blinds can be -- the curtains can be drawn up again. You may proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one or two brief questions about the compilation of the photo-boards that you looked at, that is to say the ones that you were personally reasonable for compiling. Presumably before you began, you must have had a list of the names of particular suspects that you were compiling photo-boards for?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was that a list of names given to you by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That was a list of names that kept coming up when cross-referencing all the material we had in-house and it was people that we believed may have committed crimes within our jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you do that process of selection yourself?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No, I was involved with the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this, you mentioned the provision to your team of a database of thousands of photographs that had been originally provided by the KPC, the Kosovo Protection Corps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct. I believe there were thousands. I can't say how many photographs were there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you have an impression because presumably there was a point of time at which you were just surfing through a very large number of photographs looking for people who bore a reasonable resemblance to the person whose photo-boards you were compiling?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: There were printed out copies, and I was manually going through the printed out copies and cross-referencing with the database, the electronic database.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you mentioned an international organisation that had been the conduit for the provision of those photographs from the KPC to the OTP. Now, would that be the International Organisation for Migration?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can I ask you, please, to - and I think this is clear from the evidence that you've given - but may we have it from you directly, that when compiling photo-boards that you have compiled, you never put the photograph of more than one suspect on any one photo-board?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so far as the remainder are concerned, these were people that you took from the KPC sample?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know whether the KPC sample itself was the whole of the KPC database or a random selection from it?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I am unaware of that circumstance.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally this: When you're making your selection from amongst those thousands of photographs, the only criterion you are using is that the person whose photograph you are picking out to add to the photo-board is someone who bears a sufficient similarity to the suspect that - if I can use the colloquial phrase - the suspect won't be left sticking out like a carrot in a bunch of bananas, it's a process of reasonable similarity?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They are, in effect, the equivalent random volunteers selected for a proper identification parade.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you rephrase that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They are in effect those photographs, placebos, individuals in the same position as those who would volunteer randomly volunteer for a real-life identification drill?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That was the intended effect yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- goes on, there is a matter I would like to raise with my Defence colleagues. Is it possible to take a break -- a short break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if that has to be done before --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If it suits the Chamber, it's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I don't know what you'd like to discuss with your colleagues, but the Chamber is never opposing such conversations. Then we'll have the break early, but since we started late, not at the usual time, we'll resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I was informed that you wanted to address the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the break, Mr. Re supplied us with an e-mail from investigator Thomas Obruca, dated March 15th, 2007, at 1.06 p.m., in which he says, that's Mr. Obruca, referring to Mr. Quiroz, and I quote: "Jose can't recall, and he says if it's not mentioned in the statement he does -- he does not have shown it." Now, the reason I'm raising it at this point in time is that based upon representations that were made in court on the 16th of March which were in response to some concerns the Chamber had about whether or not this person had been shown a photo-spread at all, Mr. Re made representations at page 1261, line 17, through the end, and then continuing on the next page which is: "I wish to advise you that after the matters which arose yesterday in court regarding the photo ID boards and whether or not they were shown to the witnesses, the Prosecution has conducted as thorough a search as it possibly could of all its internal records. We have reviewed our mission reports, all our statements, the photo-board, investigator notes, we can find no record of the witness being shown photo-boards which is recorded in the Office of the Prosecutor's system. The searches are ongoing but I don't think we are going to find anything, so I am putting before the Trial Chamber we have done absolutely everything we can to identify what happens and it's fairly obviously that if there had been some identification process, we surely would have had a record there somewhere," on page 1262. I don't know what further information can be obtained from investigator Obruca and whether or not -- and I haven't had the chance to go through the transcript sufficiently -- closely enough to see if there is a violation of this Court's order or not in terms of contacting the witness. But certainly there is a failure of response to this Court's order in the event that any contact was made before the Court indicated the witness and it should not have any conversations or proofing with any individuals. I don't intend to go through a lengthy examination of the witness on this issue at this time and believe that it may be appropriately raised in terms of a motion, but before I go any further, until I receive information, and that is because Mr. Re has indicated that Mr. Obruca is on compassionate leave, and he cannot confirm the correctness of what is recorded here, there still is another missing part or potentially missing part to the puzzle, and I may be reserving some cross-examination until that occurs. I'm loathed to go all the way through this examination with regard to the issue of what was learned, when, and how in the absence of having complete information for the second or third time on an issue which is of some critical importance to my client, and I wish to alert the Court to that at this time. Any motions that I might have are motions that I think I will put forth in writing as opposed to keeping on with the discussion at this time. I am deeply troubled with the way all this evidence is coming in as the Chamber can understand for obvious reasons, but that's a different issue -- or part of the same issue, but can be raised in a different matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Re, do you think that there's any -- at this time there's any need to respond to what Mr. Guy-Smith said? He mainly took it as information to the Chamber and an expression of concern, whether or not to be followed up by any further submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's an accurate indication of my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I leave it up to you whether you want to say anything about it now or whether you just wait and see what Mr. Guy-Smith will submit in the future and then to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've provided him with some information which I found while Mr. Emmerson was cross-examining. He's entitled to cross-examine on that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can't ascertain the correctness of it right at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So that's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think the witness could be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To the extent that the Prosecution was specifically ordered to deal with this issue and to the extent that the Prosecutor has an obligation not only to the Court with regard to this issue but a professional obligation to make sure that with at least with regard to this issue there is full disclosure. The question of correctness is something that could have been dealt with some time ago, specifically on the very date that Mr. Re received the e-mail. Mr. Re's failure to open up an e-mail -- Mr. Re's failure to open up an e-mail may raise some other issues, and I'm concerned about him at this point second-guessing the correctness of the e-mail that he received from his own investigator concerning a -- a conversation about something of relatively critical importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This is outrageous. I object to this. It's time for some perspective here. I was sitting in Court on that day. I didn't have access to the e-mail. Sometimes -- I remember specifically sitting where Ms. Schweiger is sitting and the thing -- not being able to open it. I found the email when I was sitting here and Mr. Emmerson was cross-examining and something jogged my memory about instructions that Mr. Reid, the deputy chief of investigations, had issued at about the time this happened. It's outrageous for Mr. Guy-Smith to say I should be opening e-mails. I'm getting over a hundred a day. Some e-mails are opened some e-mails aren't opened. The fact is something jogged my memory as I was sitting here, and I opened it, and immediately, immediately I asked for an adjournment as it is my duty to do so and communicated it to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I've got no illusion at this moment that you will agree with Mr. Guy-Smith on the matter of whether it's nice of you that you now have immediately disclosed or whether it was not nice of you not having opened it at that time. I think we leave it to the moment where any further submissions are made, outrageous or unpleasant or whatever it may be. I think at this moment the Chamber is now fully aware of the position of the two parties in this respect. Mr. Guy-Smith, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom. By the way, Mr. Troop, if I can use the time to address you just for a second. I just said well outrageous or unpleasant, perhaps last Friday I should have minded not our decision but the words in which I addressed you a bit better, and perhaps then I would have also used more pleasant words perhaps than I did. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: I don't know quite what to say, Your Honour, but thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Quiroz. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Guy-Smith, who's counsel for Mr. Balaj. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Quiroz, just so we can get to somewhat of an understanding of your experience and your qualifications, as I understand it you were an investigator and a criminal investigator for the Tribunal in East Timor, correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you were a police investigator in Spain, and you presently are a criminal investigator at the ICC; true?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And before you were an investigator for East Timor, were you involved in any police functions or investigative functions?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I worked with the Guardia Civil's [Realtime transcript read in error "Seville"] intelligence unit in Spain.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: For how long a period of time did you do that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: From 1997 to 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- perhaps for the record I usually do not correct it when we are on the go. It now reads the "Guardia Civil" where I take it it's the Guardia Civil.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you began working with Guardia Civil, did you receive training as a police officer in criminal investigations?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, in the academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When did you commence your studies with regard to criminal investigation work or police work?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I attended police -- police academy in 1994, from November 1994 to July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that then by the time you began working with the team tasked to investigate criminal activity or crimes in Kosovo, that you had been involved in the business for approximately ten years, give or take one?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. During that period of time, and by the period of time I'm referring to, that's when you were working in Guardia Civil, at that point in time did you ever use photo-boards in your investigation?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: While you were studying to become a member of the Guardia Civil, did you ever receive any classes or training with regard to the use of photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. When you left the Guardia Civil and began working at East Timor Tribunal as an investigator, did you at that time receive any training with regard to identification processes and the use of photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were working in East Timor, did you use any photo-boards or photo-spreads for purposes of identifying any potential suspects in the course of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe on some occasion I may have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say you believe on some occasion that you may have, is that some distinct memory as you sit here today, or are you speculating by virtue of the kind of cases you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No, we -- I know for a fact I did not use a photo-board as the ones that were presented here in this courtroom today. I did use photographs --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say--

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Sorry. Photographs of groups of different militias and from there people were identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that at least during East Timor experience, you at no point used the kind of photo-boards that we saw here today? I believe that's what you've just said, but I wanted to be sure.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During this time you were involved in the East Timor investigation, was there any discussion with regard to your superiors with to the utility the use of a photo-board with the purposes of identifying suspects?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After you left East Timor and you went back as a police investigator in Spain, during that period of time what kind of investigations were you engaged in, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Counter-terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Counter-terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And were part of your tasked involved in counter-terrorism the identification of potential suspects with regard to individuals who may be terrorists?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that period of time did you have occasion to use photo-boards or photo-spreads with potential witnesses in order to identify any suspects that you may have been investigating?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When did you conclude your work with the police investigators or police investigation unit in Spain?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: February 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you began working as an investigator for the ICTY, did you take any courses or seminars - I'm speaking now in a much more general sense - with regard to the kinds of investigative tasks and manner performing those tasks while working for the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you began working for the ICTY, were you tasked to a specific unit?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What unit was that?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I was -- I was assigned to the OTP, and within the OTP to a team that was investigating crimes committed in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have a team leader?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who was your team leader?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Matti Raatikainen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have discussions with Matti Raatikainen, your team leader, about the use of photo-boards as an investigative tool with regard to the investigation you were doing for crimes in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe that the issue was brought up at a team meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say the issue was brought up at a team meeting, would that have been a team meeting here in The Hague or a team meeting in Kosovo, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: It would have been in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during the time that that was brought up at a team meeting in The Hague, do you recall what was discussed?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I cannot recall right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that period of time - and by that I mean at the team meeting - do you recall whether or not there was a discussion as to how a photo-board should be comprised?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At that meeting do you recall whether or not there were any discussions concerning some of the concerns that existed generally as using a photo-board as an investigative tool?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I do not remember, but I would imagine - and I'm speculating now because --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Please don't. I don't want you to speculate. If you remember, that's fine; if you don't, so be it.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, before you came to the ICTY to work as an investigator, you had been involved in, I take it, a fair number of investigations over the years?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you have learned as an investigator, I'm sure, the importance of memorialising information concerning your efforts in that investigation; true?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's something which is not particularly unique to being a police officer, is it?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, did you have a standard method of memorialising information with regard to any investigation that you were involved in before you came to the ICTY; and by that I mean, did you have, for example, a chronological report in which you put the name, the date, the time, the individuals that you were seeking to speak to or other pertinent information?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Well, we would either do it in notebooks or electronically.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say you would do it by notebooks or electronically, I take it by that you mean by use of a computer?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that would be information that you saved?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And would ultimately then sent to either your supervising investigator or your team leader or to other individual who was in a position of authority, so they could make a determination of the use of the material; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in this situation, by that I mean in terms of your investigation in Kosovo, that's precisely what you did with regard to reports; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "I believe so," --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, you are developing a speed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you believe so, are you as you are sitting here speculating or is that what you did?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe that is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again you've used the word "believe." And I'm trying to understand each and every time you went out on an investigative mission you wrote a report about what you did, you memorialized that information in such a fashion that it would be there for eternity -- not necessarily for eternity but certainly for the purposes of the investigation that you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, those kind of reports would be distinct from the reports that we're -- that we've been talking about here, and by that I mean the statements that you took; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I do not understand exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me see if I can explain my question. It was apparently badly phrased. Sometimes you would go out into the field and you would not necessarily speak to anybody, but you would obtain information; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And specifically with regard to your investigation in the case of OTP versus Haradinaj et al., that occurred; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you specifically wrote down in a report what you did and what you learned?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I would make notes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, when you made those notes, part of the reasons you made those notes was because that was information that you could then use at a later point for investigative leads; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And also those reports were available for you to talk to your colleagues and your contemporaries about how or where the investigation should go; true?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And one of the people you would talk to, I assume, would be your team leader, Mr. Raatikainen?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And another person I take it would be Pekka Haverinen; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And who were the other people who you were involved with in your unit of investigation?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Howard Tucker, Harjit Sandhu, Ole Lehtinen, William Fulton. I'm sure there's more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sure there are, too. During the period of time that you were involved in this investigation - and I'm referring now to I believe -- I'm going to go to 2003 - during that period of time there was also an active unit or group of law enforcement people who were on the ground in Kosovo who were also engaged in investigating war crimes; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That supposedly was UNMIK?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I take it that one of the things that you would do and makes sense is that you would cross-fertilise, and by that I mean that you would share information with each other so that you could -- each group could get the benefit --

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- of the information that was being obtained from all potential sources; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as you sit here today, could you tell us some of the UNMIK individuals or UNMIK police that you dealt during the course of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to name them by names; it's been some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Would that be the kind of information that would be contained in your chronological report or the diary you referred to?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: It would probably be contained in the mission reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "mission reports," those are documents I take it that you compiled along with your fellow colleagues in the OTP and are periodically submitted to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm asking because I don't have any idea.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: It's -- was a practice when I returned from mission, and I think that other investigators did the same, was to write a report in a chronological order stating the activities that were carried out during the mission. And that was submitted to the chief of investigations through the team leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during the period of time that you were investigating in the years 2003 through 2005, was the chief of investigations for your team leader the same?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Was --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was the chief of investigations the same?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that would have been who?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That would have been Patrick Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry, I missed the last name?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Patrick Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a result of the mission reports that you compiled, did you have any meetings with Patrick Lopez-Terres concerning the manner in which you should proceed concerning your investigations?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, there were at some stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you tell us as you sit here today -- when you say "at some stage," was that in 2003? 2004? 2005? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe it was in 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that -- and as I -- and I'm -- once again, I'm guessing, when you say you believe it was in 2004, as you sit here right now today, you have no hard evidence, for example, a notebook or a diary, that would allow you to give us that information as to when you had those meetings?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No, that would be -- we would probably have minutes of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay, but you personally have no records whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No, there were team meetings with the chief of investigations or his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the mission reports that we were referring to but a moment ago, those mission reports, were those compilations that were done by all of the investigators and by that I mean some of the individuals you've mentioned like Mr. Tucker and Mr. Lehtinen or were those a compilation that you received from your colleagues at UNMIK?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were the mission -- the reports --

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- were those reports something that were a compilation of all the investigative efforts of all the individuals?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: The nature of the mission report itself would be -- let's say a log of activities that were carried out. Meetings with different agencies, different people on the ground, that would have been recorded in individual notes to file, investigator's notes to file, which would be circulated as well for everybody's attention within the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that -- there's a sensible reason for doing that, that's so everybody can share the same body of information and understand where the progress of the investigation is going; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were a police officer before you became working for international organisations, did you have occasion in interviewing witnesses to video record any witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That was not the nature of my duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you started taking statements, I guess that would be first of all probably when you were in East Timor?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you started taking statements in East Timor at that point in time, did you begin utilising the method of video recording as a way of memorialising statements so that you would have available to you a complete, accurate statement, both of word and of demeanour?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No, that was not used.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you audio-record?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you get handwritten statements from some of those people?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And by "handwritten statement," that is a statement where the actual -- the individual that you were talking to writes out in their own hand that which occurred?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Or that which they are reporting?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Or the individual would have handed a handwritten statement made prior by themselves to me to channelize through the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: By the time that you got to Kosovo, did things change? Were you using video recordings by then?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Some video recordings were used in suspect -- audio mostly, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I heard you use the word "suspect" --

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Suspect interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from suspects, was it your unit's practice to video or audio record other witnesses who were important to the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I don't recall any.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall there being any discussions about when it would be appropriate to video record, audio record, or take a written statement from a suspect, the distinct between the three? Do you recall whether or not your unit had any discussions about when you would choose to do one or the other?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "no" is that because it's something you don't remember or it's something you believe never occurred?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: The only time I do remember audio recording or video recording was in the case of suspects' interviews; in all other cases, I don't remember it being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And you personally never recorded any interviews unless -- and by "record," I mean audio recorded any interviews unless they dealt with a suspect?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you were involved in an investigative task of interviewing with one of your colleagues, the same would be true?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. How did you get the job of having to go through thousands of photos to put together the photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I have absolutely no idea. I was tasked with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were tasked with it. Okay. Now, that is something that I, as I understand your testimony, took you a period of some weeks to do?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: The whole process, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the whole process, that means for all of the individuals who you've identified that you put together photo-boards for, that's Ramush Haradinaj, Lahi Brahimaj, Nazmi Brahimaj, Daut Haradinaj, Alush Agushi, and Pjeter Shala?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, did you do that by yourself? By that, I mean did you compile the photo-boards for each one of those individuals by yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After you got the pictures?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes. I don't remember if I did it by myself or somebody else assisted me on some occasion, but I believe I did do it by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There clearly would be -- when you were doing that particular task there would be some log of the efforts of how you put the photo-board together?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There would be a record of what you did --

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: The record --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The record, which is that you picked this photo --

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I picked the photographs, it would be mostly on e-mail exchange, I guess, that I had with the mapping and printing unit. Once I compiled the photographs, I sent them up to the mapping and printing unit and back. Once I had the results, I presented them to -- in a team meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say you presented them in a team meeting, of all the individuals who were in the team meeting, were those people that you referred to before who were familiar with the suspects you were investigating?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did Mr. -- I have a hard time with his name Matti Raatikainen?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Matti Raatikainen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Discuss with you any guide-lines that should be used --

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- for purposes of compiling the photo-spread?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Standard operational procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "standard operational procedures," that is something that the two of you discussed together or were you relying on something?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: I was asked to compile suspected photo-boards or photo-boards according to the protocol, SOP, that I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: And I found the SOP in a book where it was a compendium of all protocols and procedures that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter I believe it's -- it's not 65 ter, it's Defence 633 called up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Hopefully a document will, if I have done it properly, will pop up in a moment and it's called "Identification Guide-lines." Now, is this the standard operating procedure document that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this is the document you would reviewed before you began to compile the photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could I have a -- it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. Re. Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, when you went -- after you compiled the photo-boards that you told us about in this case, you had them -- so I'm clear about how it was done, you had them sent to mapping?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: They produced three separate copies for you of each suspect with seven foils?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE QUIROZ
utterances.text: Yes.
